subject: DONE s319: list-assignment in list ctx must return LVALUES — odd hash tail + greedy-starved scalar returned bare undef (hashassign.t t304 + aassign.t ×6)
description:
DONE s319.  Found via #162's near-green batch; the diagnosis generalised further
than the rows that prompted it.

PERL'S RULE: a list assignment evaluated in list context returns its TARGETS as
lvalues, so `$_++ foreach (LIST) = (VALUES)` increments the real variables.

TWO sites handed back a VALUE where an lvalue box was required, so the write
landed in a temporary and the variable kept its old value — silently:

 1. `p-hash-fill` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) stored the ODD TRAILING key's padded
    value as a bare `*p-undef*`, while every other value went through
    `%p-make-hash-entry` (which boxes).  `$_++ foreach %h = (1,2,3)` therefore
    could not write the padded value.  -> op/hashassign.t t304.
 2. `p-list-=`'s post-greedy collect pushed `*p-undef*` for a scalar target
    STARVED by a greedy array/hash, instead of that variable's own box.  So $z
    in `($x,$y,%h,$z) = (0)` never saw the ++.  -> perl-tests/aassign.t ×6.

Both fixes route through the mechanism that already existed rather than adding a
branch (CLAUDE.md 11): site 1 now calls the same %p-make-hash-entry as its
sibling; site 2 pushes `,var` (the box the assign form just set to undef).

SCOPE CORRECTION (I first claimed t307-309 too — they are NOT fixed): those
three rows still fail, but NOT because this fix is incomplete.  The assigned
VALUES are already correct — a probe of `($x,$y,%h,$z) = (0)` flattens
byte-identically to perl.  They fail because the test asserts
`eq_array([$x,$y,%h,$z], [...])`, and building that ARRAYREF LITERAL hits a
separate, PRE-EXISTING bug: a hash inside a parenthesised list literal is not
flattened (task #170, verified identical at HEAD).  op/hashassign.t is 306/3.

VERIFIED:
 - 6-case parity probe vs perl 5.40.3: byte-identical, including the cases that
   already worked (guard against over-correcting).
 - Gate 124 files / 4456 tests PASS (4453 + 3 new).
 - Full sweep: **0 new**, 7 blessed failures FIXED — hashassign.t t304 plus SIX
   aassign.t "lval: c post [012] XY[AH]Z" rows, the same starved-scalar shape.
   Baseline 698 -> 691 by a SURGICAL edit of exactly those 7 rows; a wholesale
   re-bless would have written 688 and silently deleted the 3 rows
   eval.t/postfixderef.t did not run (PARTIAL).
 - Regression guard: new Pl/t/transpile-test-08.t (-06 at the ~50 cap, -07 past
   it), 3 tests incl. inverse checks — padded key still exists() and reads
   undef, returned values NOT aliased to the RHS.

NO cache-generation bump: runtime-only semantics, emission unchanged.

GOTCHA for whoever greps docs/fail-baseline.tsv: it contains NUL bytes, so plain
grep treats it as binary and prints NOTHING.  Use `grep -a`.
